headings.title: SMTO-EXE-0219 — SMTO can't make this change to this kind of PDF

html:
SMTO-EXE-0219 — SMTO can't make this change to this kind of PDF

GUID: 8756972e-3599-5021-a68d-420f10384888
Slug: pdf-unsupported-feature
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: pdf

What happened

  • This PDF uses something SMTO can't safely edit, such as a digital signature, a special dynamic form or a password field. SMTO stopped before making a new file, and your original PDF is unchanged.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If the PDF is digitally signed, ask the sender for an unsigned copy, or make the change in the app that was used to sign it. SMTO won't edit signed PDFs, because any change would break the signature.
  2. If you're combining or inserting pages from several PDFs, use copies without password protection, if you're allowed to, then ask SMTO again. SMTO can't combine password-protected PDFs, because each file's protection can't be safely merged into one.
  3. If you're filling a form, use values that exactly match the field's choices, and leave password and signature fields empty. SMTO only fills text boxes, checkboxes and choice lists, and only with values the form itself offers.
  4. If the form only works properly in Adobe Reader, fill it in there instead. Such dynamic forms build themselves while open, and SMTO only edits standard PDF forms.

What success looks like

  • SMTO creates the new PDF and tells you where it saved it.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with what you asked SMTO to do, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't try to strip a signature or protection from a document you aren't allowed to change.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway PDF backend refused the change because the document uses an unsupported feature: an XFA form, a signature field, a password or unsupported form field, a value not offered by the field, a multi-file operation on an encrypted PDF, or an invalid attachment or field edit.

What this means

  • The requested transform encountered XFA, signature-bearing content, unsupported/password form fields or an encrypted multi-source transformation it cannot safely support. PDF parsing and OCR remain local bounded operations on the selected Gateway. Outputs are separate create-only files/artifacts; diagnostic rendering adds no reads, credential recovery, model calls or automatic retries.

Why this can happen

  • The requested transform encountered XFA, signature-bearing content, unsupported/password form fields or an encrypted multi-source transformation it cannot safely support.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect form/encryption/signature metadata and the exact transformation without dropping unsupported features silently.

How to fix it

  • Find which check fired in src/gateway_core/pdf/backend.py (Document.writable, Document.fields, transform, fill or edit_field). Use an unsigned static AcroForm PDF, supply values that exist in the field's options or appearance states, avoid multi-file operations on encrypted inputs, and handle XFA or signing in an external PDF tool; SMTO does not support those cases.
  • Use a supported static PDF/AcroForm. XFA, signing, password-field mutation and multi-source encrypted transforms are unsupported.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use a supported static PDF/AcroForm. XFA, signing, password-field mutation and multi-source encrypted transforms are unsupported.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported static PDF/AcroForm operation preserves required content, or a trusted external workflow handles the unsupported feature.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay uncertain writes or execute embedded document content.

Technical notes

  • PDF parsing and OCR remain local bounded operations on the selected Gateway. Outputs are separate create-only files/artifacts; diagnostic rendering adds no reads, credential recovery, model calls or automatic retries.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
